summary: A tide pool at dusk that happens to contain a sorting puzzle — light inside glass on deep water, a keeper's voice, a win that is a sun over a lit rack — and the first app here whose ladder can prove it is still climbing at rung 200, though nothing it records about the player ever changes what it deals next.
fixes: Make the pour look like a pour: source travel 0.34 -> 0.62 and rise unit*0.62 -> unit*1.15 (BoardView.swift:201), pourDuration 0.24 -> 0.34 s (Palette.swift:124), and hold `stream` through the landing instead of fading it at GameModel.swift:253 — ten moment-pour frames currently show no stream at all.

Retime the win moment (qa.json moments[1]: delay 2.2 -> 0.8, interval 0.12, frames 12) and deal on the calling actor under Motion.isStill (GameModel.swift:115) so moment-win stops being ten identical frames and ax-01-win stops being the dealing screen.
Wrap each vial in a Button with .buttonStyle(.pressable) and Haptics.soft() on finger-down — BoardView.swift:168 is a bare .onTapGesture, so nothing answers under the thumb until the finger lifts.

Put what playing opens on the Shore: a band drawn from AppInfo.earned above the paid toggles, lit at 31/125/200 with the next one named, so PacksView stops being a screen where every door is a purchase.

Read what the app already records: draw an over-par rack as half-lit glass on the shelf and offer 'Walk rack 23 again — you were four over' on the win, since LevelResult stores moves against par (Results.swift:7) and nothing consults it.

Break the plateau at racks 31-124 (one shape, bar 28, ninety-four times): move the depth dial in (opensAt 45, every 40) or open a fourth dimension around rack 60, and fix the three comments still claiming depth changes at 45/50.
Balance the rack rows in BoardView.swift:96 — eleven vials lay out 5/5/1 and the last one floats alone in a half-screen of empty water.
